concepts.name: Two-Dimensional Shapes
concepts.description: Students observe common objects and identify basic two-dimensional shapes such as triangles, squares, rectangles, circles, and polygons. They relate geometric shapes to their everyday surroundings.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to identify and classify common two-dimensional shapes found in their surroundings.

concepts.name: Properties of Shapes
concepts.description: Each geometric shape has unique characteristics based on its sides, corners, and angles. Understanding these properties helps distinguish one shape from another.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to compare geometric shapes based on the number of sides, vertices, and angles.

concepts.name: Angle as a Measure of Turn
concepts.description: An angle represents the amount of turning between two rays meeting at a common point. Students explore angles through body movements, doors, clocks, and rotating objects.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to recognize angles as measures of turning in everyday situations.

concepts.name: Parts of an Angle
concepts.description: Every angle consists of a vertex and two arms. These components help describe and compare different angles.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to identify the vertex and arms of an angle.

concepts.name: Comparing Angles
concepts.description: Angles can be compared visually without measurement by observing the amount of opening between their arms.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to compare two angles and identify which is larger or smaller.

concepts.name: Right Angle
concepts.description: A right angle measures exactly 90° and serves as a reference for identifying other types of angles.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to identify right angles in geometric figures and real-life objects.

concepts.name: Acute and Obtuse Angles
concepts.description: Angles smaller than a right angle are acute angles, while those larger than a right angle but smaller than a straight angle are obtuse angles.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to classify angles as acute, right, or obtuse.

concepts.name: Straight Angle
concepts.description: A straight angle forms a straight line and measures 180°. It helps students understand angle relationships.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to recognize and identify straight angles.

concepts.name: Shape Patterns
concepts.description: Repeated arrangements of shapes create geometric patterns found in rangoli, tiles, fabrics, and architecture.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to identify and extend patterns formed using geometric shapes.

concepts.name: Symmetry in Shapes
concepts.description: Many shapes exhibit symmetry, where one half mirrors the other. Symmetry is common in nature, art, and design.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to identify lines of symmetry in simple geometric figures.

concepts.name: Practical Applications of Geometry
concepts.description: Knowledge of shapes and angles is applied in construction, drawing, design, and everyday problem-solving.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to relate geometric concepts to practical situations in daily life.

concepts.name: Understanding Shapes and Angles
concepts.description: This chapter develops students' understanding of geometric shapes, angle types, symmetry, and spatial reasoning through observation and hands-on activities.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to identify, compare, classify, and apply knowledge of shapes and angles to solve elementary geometry problems.
